title: Python Warmup: Strings, Comprehensions, and Euclidean Distance
description: Use an f-string, a generator expression with sum(), and a Euclidean distance function to run three quick Python snippets.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex + split: claude

steps.description: Import `math`, bind `course = "CS477"`, and print a greeting using an f-string.
Create the 3-element list `rooms = ["dirty", "clean", "dirty"]` and count how many entries equal `"dirty"` using `sum(1 for r in rooms if r == "dirty")`.
Define `distance(p, q)` to pair coordinates with `zip(p, q)` and sum their squared differences `(a - b) ** 2`. Take the square root with `math.sqrt`, then call `distance((0, 0), (3, 4))`.
Look at line 14. `zip(p, q)` pairs `0` with `3` and `0` with `4`, so the generator yields `(0 - 3) ** 2` and `(0 - 4) ** 2`. Then `sum` and `math.sqrt` run.

steps.question: What two numbers do lines 10 and 16 print for `score` and `distance((0, 0), (3, 4))`?
steps.answer: Line 10 prints `2` (two `"dirty"` rooms), and line 16 prints `5.0` (`math.sqrt(9 + 16)`).

steps.description: After checking all three elements of `rooms`, `score` is `2` and line 10 prints `Rooms the agent can clean: 2`.
